title: Henselian colimit for the pair henselization category
statement: For a commutative ring B and ideal J, let C be the full category of ring maps B to D with Spec(D) to Spec(B) etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the canonical map B/J to D/JD bijective, with all B-algebra maps as morphisms. There is a colimit cocone in rings under B, with vertex B to H, such that (H,JH) is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and the canonical map B/J to H/JH is bijective.

proof.text: Use essential smallness and filteredness. Transfer preservation of filtered colimits by the ring forgetful functor along equivSmallModel. Mathlib hasColimitsOfShape_of_essentiallySmall supplies ring colimits, and connectedness supplies colimits in the under category. Choose colimit.cocone for the full inclusion.

For each stage invert the canonical quotient isomorphism and compose with the quotient projection. Maps from a stage to B/J fixing B uniquely factor through that quotient, so these maps form a cocone. Its induced map pi : H to B/J kills JH and gives a left inverse to B/J to H/JH, proving injectivity. For surjectivity represent an element of H at a stage, lift its class modulo JC from B/J, and apply the quotient map induced by its coprojection. The under-category commutativity identifies the result with the canonical image in H/JH.

Apply pair_henselization_sections to this cocone, its colimit proof, and the proved quotient bijection. Then apply henselianRing_of_etale_section_lifting in universes u,u and take its henselian conjunct. Assemble the cocone, colimit witness, henselian proof and quotient bijection.

lean.statement: theorem pair_henselization_colimit (B : Type u) [CommRing B] (J : Ideal B) : ∃ c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of B) ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J.map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map)))), Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ HenselianRing c.pt.right (J.map c.pt.hom.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J.map c.pt.hom.hom) c.pt.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map))
